'''Abraham''' or '''Abram Robertson''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (4 November 1751 – 4 December 1826), was a [[Scotland|Scottish]] [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]]. He held the [[Savilian chair of geometry|Savilian Chair of Geometry]] at the  [[University of Oxford]] from  1797 to 1809.

Robertson was born at [[Duns, Scottish Borders|Duns]], [[Berwickshire]], the son of Abraham Robertson, “a man of humble station”. He attended school at Great Ryle in [[Northumberland]], and later at Duns. At age 24, he moved to [[London]], he had hopes of travelling to the [[East Indies]], but his patron died. During the 1770s, Robertson completed a [[Bachelor of Arts]] and Master in Arts.

In 1795, the [[Royal Society]] elected him a [[Fellow of the Royal Society|fellow]] in recognition of his work on conic sections.

In 1792, Robertson published ''Sectionum conicarum libri septem''.
